catalog_title: Subdiffusive and KPZ passage-time fluctuation exponents

original_source.authors: Antonio Auffinger, Michael Damron, Jack Hanson
original_source.title: 50 years of first passage percolation
original_source.location: Question 13 and related Question 15, PDF printed p.36; also summary of open questions printed p.145
original_source.short_quote: under suitable conditions on F, chi < 1/2. If d = 2, show that chi = 1/3

mathematical_scope.model: Undirected nearest-neighbour Z^d FPP with iid nonnegative edge weights tau_e of law F and point-to-point passage time T(x,y).
mathematical_scope.source_question: Question 13 asks for suitable conditions on F under which chi<1/2 for every d>=2 and chi=1/3 for d=2. Question 15 separately asks for chi>0 in suitable dimensions. The canonical P0104 store concept combines these source questions; the P0104 catalog title emphasizes Question 13.
unfixed_by_source: The exact definition of chi and meaning of variance asymptotics: survey p.34 says the meaning of the approximate scaling symbol was not fixed.
The phrase suitable conditions on F leaves moment, nondegeneracy, and limit-shape regularity hypotheses to be chosen.
mathematical_scope.operational_surrogate_not_claimed_as_ori: For a specified nondegenerate bounded continuous planar edge law F, establish existence of chi_var(F,e1)=lim_n log Var(T(0,n e1))/(2 log n) and its value 1/3; a law-specific result would still require care about the source's universality claim.

primary_literature_checked.result: Damron-Hanson-Sosoe proved O(n/log n) variance under 2+log moment assumptions, not a strict power exponent.
Damron-Hanson-Sosoe proved exponential concentration on sqrt(n/log n) scale under an exponential moment assumption.
Basu-Sidoravicius-Sly report O(n^(1-epsilon)) variance for a rotationally invariant planar Riemannian model, not the iid lattice model in Question 13.
Chatterjee proves the conditional KPZ scaling relation if exponents exist in his sense; it does not establish chi=1/3.
